\[
\hat{f}(x,y) = g(x,y) - \min\Bigl(1,\, \frac{\sigma_\eta^2}{\sigma_L^2}\Bigr)\bigl[g(x,y) - m_L\bigr]
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(g\): The noisy image
- \(m_L\): The local mean
- \(\sigma_L^2\): The local variance
- \(\sigma_\eta^2\): The noise variance

g is the noisy image, m_L and sigma_L squared are the mean and variance of the window, and sigma_eta squared is the noise variance. If the local variance is near the noise variance, the ratio is near 1 and the output is the local mean. If the local variance is much larger, the ratio is small and the pixel is kept. Gonzalez and Woods limit the ratio to 1 when the noise variance is larger. That makes this the same estimator as the adaptive Wiener filter of Lee, written in another form.
